chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a woman, and she bore him a girl, then the woman died, so he married another, and she bore him a child, then indeed she breastfed a boy from her milk. Is it permissible for that boy whom she breastfed to marry the daughter of the woman who was under the man's guardianship before the last woman? He said, 'I like that the son of a bull (male) who has sucked from its milk should not marry its daughter.'

key_terms.ابْنَةَ فَحْل: son of a bull (metaphor for male offspring)

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of the woman who breastfed him?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the scope of *radāʿ* (breastfeeding) kinship, establishing that a wet-nurse creates a maternal bond with her wet-nurse's children, thereby prohibiting their marriage. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs a metaphorical analogy—comparing the wet-nurse to a 'female stallion' (or mother) and the wet-nurse's child to her offspring—to illustrate that the prohibition extends to the daughter of the woman who breastfed him, reinforcing the principle that *radāʿ* creates a permanent marital barrier similar to consanguinity.
